title: Harvard plates with 56 control stars confirm the 1937 and 1981 occultations of ASASSN-24fw: P = 15,998.5 d, and the 1937 event had the 2024-25 duration within 5 percent
abstract: Question: is the 43.8-year period of the deep occultation star ASASSN-24fw (Gaia DR3 3152916838954800512) real when the noise of the Harvard plates is calibrated, and did the earlier events have the 2024-25 timing and duration? Method: DASCH DR7 plate light curves (1889-1990) of the star and of 56 plate-matched control stars of the same brightness and colour; a censored likelihood with detections and plate limits; the 2024 ingress from ZTF and ASAS-SN as the event template. Results: with no period assumed, the two strongest events in 100 years of target plates are at ingress 1937.11 (dlnL 38.2) and 1980.87 (16.5); the strongest event of any control is 12.1. A blind period scan (2,000-45,000 d) gives P = 15,998.5 d (dlnL 54.8; controls at most 16.3; robust to six analysis variants). The 1937 plates record the ingress (0.40 and 0.80 mag fades 4.2 d apart, as the 2024 template predicts), 8 deep non-detections while 83-96 percent of controls are seen, and the egress. A free fit gives P = 15,998.5 d (95 percent 15,997.3-15,999.3) and a 1937 duration of 261 d (250-265), equal to the 2024-25 value (250-257 d) within about 5 percent. The 1981 timing agrees with one constant period. ZTF shows that the star returned to its pre-event brightness to within 0.004 mag. APPLAUSE plates are too shallow and miss both windows. Limitations: the 2024-25 egress uses published dates because ZTF has a gap; the plates are B-like and the template is ZTF g; the 1893 window has only shallow plates. Next ingress: about 2068 July 6.
